subtype: Approach: makes big decisions while angry or anxious [Pitfall]
passage:
Urmila: You once told me you almost left engineering. What happened?

Vasudev: The mechanics result came out and I had failed. My friends were all fine. I walked home shaking, opened the transfer form and filled it in that same night. All I could think was: everyone has seen it, I'm the stupid one. The next morning I snapped at my adviser and said I was dropping the branch. A week later, in the canteen, I actually looked at my marks. I had passed every other subject. One paper. And what I was running from was not the branch. It was everyone seeing me fail. I had nearly changed my whole life to hide from a feeling.

Urmila: Did you send the form?

Vasudev: No. But I had to go back and apologise to my adviser first.

qa.q: What did Vasudev find on looking at the marks a week later?
qa.a: Vasudev had passed every other subject, with only one paper failed.

qa.q: What was Vasudev feeling when filling in the transfer form?
qa.a: Vasudev felt ashamed and angry, thinking everyone had seen the failure.

qa.q: What could Vasudev have done on the night of the result?
qa.a: Vasudev could have waited a few days, looked at all the marks and talked with the adviser before any big decision.

qa.q: How might the adviser have felt when snapped at?
qa.a: The adviser may have felt surprised and concerned, until Vasudev came back to apologise.

grounding: Shows Vasudev deciding in anger and shame to drop the branch and later seeing the choice was driven by the feeling.

subtype: Approach: makes big decisions while angry or anxious [Pitfall]
passage: I'm Sonali. My brother Irfan came home from college the day the semester results came out. He'd failed one paper and scraped through two. He threw his bag on the sofa and said, "I'm dropping mechanical. I'm switching to commerce. I'm filling the form tonight." His voice was shaking and his ears were red. Ammi tried to talk; he walked out. I saw him at the laptop at midnight, typing fast. A week later I found him on the terrace, calmer. He said quietly, "I didn't hate the subject. I just couldn't bear everyone seeing that mark." He hadn't sent the form, luckily. But he told me he'd spent the week too embarrassed to answer his friends.

qa.q: How many papers did Irfan fail?
qa.a: He failed one paper and scraped through two.

qa.q: Why did Irfan really want to drop mechanical, looking back?
qa.a: He felt ashamed and angry about the result; a week later he saw he didn't hate the subject but couldn't bear people seeing the mark.

qa.q: What would you advise Irfan if a bad result comes again?
qa.a: Wait a few days before any big decision and talk it through with a teacher or advisor once calm, so facts decide, not shame.

qa.q: How did Ammi likely feel when Irfan walked out?
qa.a: She probably felt worried and hurt, wanting to help but shut out.

grounding: After a poor result, a student decides in a rage to drop his branch; a week later, calmer, he sees shame drove the choice.

subtype: Approach: makes big decisions while angry or anxious [Pitfall]
passage:
Monday: The results went up on the portal. Tanvir had a backlog in thermodynamics. He slammed his laptop shut, stormed to the hostel office and asked for the branch-change form. "I'm done with this branch," he told Alka on the phone, almost shouting. She asked him to wait. He hung up.

Thursday: He filled half the form and stopped at the reason box. He couldn't write "I'm embarrassed". He wrote nothing.

The following Monday: Walking back from the canteen with Alka, much calmer, he said, "I'd have switched because I was ashamed. Not because I don't like it. I actually like the design subjects." He tore up the form. That afternoon he booked a meeting with his faculty advisor about clearing the backlog.

qa.q: Which subject did Tanvir get a backlog in?
What was Tanvir feeling when he stopped at the reason box on Thursday?
qa.a: He felt too embarrassed to write the real reason, and was starting to sense that shame, not dislike, was driving him.

qa.q: What else could Tanvir have done on Monday?
qa.a: He could have given himself a few days and spoken to his faculty advisor before asking for any form.

qa.q: How might Alka have felt when Tanvir hung up on her?
qa.a: Alka was probably worried and a little hurt, since she only asked him to wait.

grounding: A student decides in anger to leave his branch after a poor result; a week later, calmer, he sees shame drove the choice.
